statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve defined by x^{5}-6xy-y^{2} = 9 at the point ( 1,-4 ).
The slope of the curve at the point (1, -4) is .

solution.p: Differentiating implicitly with respect to x gives 5x^{4}-6y-6x\, \frac{dy}{dx}-2y\, \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, or -\left(6x+2y\right)\, \frac{dy}{dx} = -(5x^{4}-6y), and so \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{5x^{4}-6y}{6x+2y}. Hence, the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the given point is \frac{dy}{dx} \bigg \vert _ {(x, y) = (1, -4)} = \frac{5\cdot 1^{4}-6\cdot \left(-4\right)}{6\cdot 1+2\cdot \left(-4\right)} \textstyle =-\frac{29}{2} .
